Its keyboard spans three octaves and sounds one note at a time, while a knob extends the range to eight octaves; the keyboard hangs on springs and is rocked sideways to give a natural vibrato, it is touch-sensitive, and the volume is controlled by a knee lever. 昂迪歐琳琴主要由真空管、電子元件與金屬構件組成。樂器外殼採用木製框架與金屬面板，: The Ondioline is built mainly from valves, electronic components and metal parts. The casing has a wooden frame and a metal panel, and the keyboard is made of keys in ivory or plastic. Inside are valve oscillator circuits, resistors, capacitors and other analogue electronic parts, together with a built-in amplifier and speaker. The stop knobs are made of metal and plastic. To keep the cost down Jenny often used low-grade parts and salvaged materials, so the instrument needs regular maintenance.
昂迪歐琳琴曾出現在流行歌曲伴奏、錄音室製作、電影配樂與搖滾錄音中。它用於夏爾·特: The Ondioline has appeared in pop-song backing, studio production, film scores and rock recordings. It is used on Charles Trenet's song L'âme des poètes, on Kai Winding's More, on Terry Stafford's Suspicion, and on two hits by Tommy James and the Shondells. Motown also used it in place of expensive string sections on several early recordings. In serious music there is a Suite Op.59 written for three Ondiolines, and the solo pieces Musette and Eolus.
昂迪歐琳琴為單音電鳴鍵盤樂器，鍵盤原為三個八度，經音域旋鈕可達八個八度。其振盪器: The Ondioline is a monophonic electrophone keyboard instrument; the keyboard was originally three octaves and a range knob takes it to eight. Its oscillator uses a multivibrator circuit to produce a pulse waveform, and that passes through ten to seventeen sliders, switches and continuous analogue controls on the filter panel, so that it can imitate orchestral instruments such as the oboe and the French horn fairly closely, or produce sounds that imitate nothing. The keyboard is pressure-sensitive and pressing a key sideways gives a natural vibrato; the volume is controlled by a knee lever. A strip can also be pressed for a percussion effect. Compared with the Ondes Martenot, which sounds on the theremin principle and offers fewer tone colours, the Ondioline has more filtering and more controls, hence richer overtones and a wider range of timbres.
昂迪歐琳琴由法國人 Georges Jenny 於 1939 年構想，當時他在法: The Ondioline was conceived by the Frenchman Georges Jenny in 1939, while he was ill in a sanatorium in the south of France, and he built the prototype with a valve system. In 1946 his working model won first prize in the invention competition at the Paris trade fair, and in 1947 the instrument was named and commercial manufacture began. Jenny kept revising it at his Paris company, so there is no single standard model, and later versions added automatic vibrato and tremolo; to bring the price down he often used low-grade parts, and the instrument needs regular maintenance. About 1,200 were made from the middle of the 1940s to the late 1960s, mostly by hand, and kits and plans were also offered. Jean-Jacques Perrey promoted it by playing, recording and selling it, which carried it into pop music and film scores.
此電鳴鍵盤樂器源自法國，演奏時以右手按鍵演奏旋律，左手調整音域旋鈕，使三個八度鍵: This electrophone keyboard instrument comes from France. The right hand plays the melody on the keys while the left works the range knob, extending the three-octave keyboard to eight octaves; at the same time the sliders and switches on the filter panel are used to change the timbre. The volume is controlled by a knee lever, the keyboard is pressure-sensitive, and pressing a key and shifting it sideways gives a natural vibrato. A strip can also be pressed for a percussion effect. A beginner can start with a single-line melody in the right hand and range and filter changes in the left, then steady the volume with the knee lever; the instrument sounds one note at a time and is not suited to playing chords.
